intro: Lazur is an AI assistant for facilities managers on Mac. Hold Option and Command, ask about what is on your screen, and Lazur answers out loud. It helps with work orders, vendor email and Excel maintenance sheets, but it does not click or edit for you. This page covers where a facilities manager's time goes, what to ask, and the limits you should know before you rely on it.
tldr: Lazur is a voice assistant for Mac. It looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut, and it answers out loud.
A 2025 VTS survey found work orders, invoices and vendor coordination are the top time drains for property teams. It counts shares, not hours.
Use Lazur for guidance in Excel and Outlook, drafts, dictation and research. It does not click buttons or change files for you.

blocks.text: What an AI assistant for facilities managers does on a Mac

A facilities manager keeps a building running. Work orders come in from tenants and staff. Vendors send invoices. Preventive maintenance schedules live in spreadsheets. An AI assistant for this job has to work where that work already happens, which is Outlook, Excel, Word and the browser.

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold Option and Command to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and it draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

That last part matters. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app. You make every change. Your job is still to know what the change should be.
Where a facilities manager's day goes, based on the research

Start with the honest version. No study measures how many hours facilities managers spend on email, admin or typing. The Bureau of Labor Statistics says these managers spend much of their day in an office. Its duties list does not mention computers, email or software. So the figures below come from nearby roles. Read them as patterns, not as your timesheet.

headers: Share naming it a top time drain
rows: More than 400 property managers and business leaders
blocks.caption: Shares name each task as a top time drain, not hours. Source: Facilities Dive on the VTS 2025 Global Workplace Report.

blocks.text: Read the table as a ranking. The survey asked people to name their top time drains. It did not ask for minutes. It also covers property managers and business leaders, which is close to your work but not the same job.

A few more numbers add context. Property managers average five operational systems and three reporting tools a day. About one-third say they lose time to data that does not match across those systems. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index reports an average of 117 emails received per day for knowledge workers. Most of those emails get skimmed in under 60 seconds. That is a general office figure, but it describes the inbox you live in.
Work order management on Mac: AI help with requests and vendor email

Start with the work order queue. The survey gives it the highest share of any task. A lot of that queue is reading, sorting and replying. Lazur helps with the reading and the reply. You still decide what gets fixed, by whom and when.

items: Hold Option and Command and ask what the status on screen means, and what the next step is. Lazur reads the screen and answers out loud.
Ask Lazur to point at the asset ID, the location and the requester's name, so you copy each one correctly into the vendor email.
Hold fn and dictate a short reason for the delay. Lazur types clean text at the cursor in the app you are using.
Ask Lazur to draft the vendor reply in a plain tone. Check the dates, asset IDs and part numbers yourself.
Save the reply as a draft in Outlook. Send it after a second read.

blocks.text: Be strict with the draft. A draft can sound right and still name the wrong floor or the wrong date. Read it aloud once. Voice tools make small slips, and a wrong floor sends a vendor to the wrong door.
Excel for facilities managers on Mac: PM schedules, invoices and spend

Preventive maintenance schedules are where many facilities managers lose time. A sheet with assets down the side, service dates across the top and a Next Due column works well. It stops working when someone changes a row and nobody checks the formulas. Lazur helps you read and repair that sheet without memorizing every function.

Here is a worked example. Your chillers need quarterly service. The Next Due column holds dates, and you want overdue rows to stand out. Hold Option and Command and ask which rows are due before today. Lazur points at the column and reads the matches. Then ask for a guided walk through a highlight rule.

In Excel for Mac, the path is Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules > Less Than. Lazur guides each click. It can also explain why a rule that compares against =TODAY() updates on its own each day. Check first that the column holds real dates. Right-click the column and choose Format Cells to confirm the format. Text that looks like a date will not compare correctly.

Invoices need the same care. Ask Lazur to explain a total before you trust it. Ask what a SUMIFS formula is doing, part by part. It explains out loud. Then test the formula on one vendor whose invoices you already know.

Microsoft's release notes list Office for Mac 16.114.3 as the latest release, dated October 27, 2026. Your copy may be older. Check Excel > About Excel. For the full sheet layout, see [Excel for facilities managers on Mac](/for/facilities-managers/excel).
Outlook for facilities managers on Mac: shared inboxes, vendor threads and rooms

Many facilities teams use a shared inbox for requests. Vendor threads, room bookings and approvals often sit in the same place. Lazur can point to the folder, the reply button or the setting. It does not change any of them for you.

Check your Outlook version before you follow any steps. Microsoft says the legacy Outlook for Mac client stops working against Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. The Exchange Web Services that client depends on retires October 1, 2026. That date has passed as of this writing. The replacement is the latest Outlook for Mac. To switch, turn off the Legacy Outlook toggle. Exchange SE on-premises mailboxes keep legacy support until October 9, 2029.

For the shared inbox setup, read [how to add a shared mailbox in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/add-a-shared-mailbox-in-outlook). For daily habits, the [Outlook page for facilities managers](/for/facilities-managers/outlook) covers rooms and templates.
A useful habit is a small set of reply templates with clear names. Ask Lazur to draft the subject line and the first paragraph. Then add the details yourself, every time.
Word and dictation for walk-throughs, SOPs and punch lists

Walk-throughs produce notes in a pocket, on a clipboard or in a phone. Hold fn and speak. Lazur dictates clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. You can save snippets, add words to a personal dictionary and keep clipboard slots. A site code or a contractor's name becomes one short phrase.

Word is where procedures live. Before you format a long SOP, ask Lazur to point at the Header option on the Insert tab. [How to add a header in Word on Mac](/how-to/add-a-header-in-word) covers the steps. Page numbers follow the same pattern, so see [how to add page numbers in Word on Mac](/how-to/add-page-numbers-in-word) when you need them.

Dictation works well for long notes. Check names, part numbers and room codes before the note goes out. If you want to test your own typing speed first, try the [typing speed test](/tools/typing-speed-test).
Research on vendors, permits and local rules

Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Use the output to gather candidates and sources. Do not use it as the final answer.

Here is a real use. You need a roof repair quote, and you want a shortlist. Ask Lazur to research roofing contractors in your city and compare their published service areas. Then open each vendor's own site. Check licensing and the pricing page yourself. You may find no published price at all. Write that in your notes, and ask for a written quote.

Permit and code questions need the official source. Ask Lazur to pull the city or county pages on parking garage repairs. Then read them with your engineer or permit office. Lazur finds pages. It does not sign off on work.
Privacy, tenant data and your employer's rules

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to get an answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Memory of what you asked stays on your Mac.

That does not decide what you may paste in. Work orders can carry tenant names, phone numbers and access notes. HR files and badge records carry staff data. If you manage a hospital, school or clinic, patient or student information may sit near your screen. Follow your employer's rules on that data before you use any AI tool with it. Ask IT or your data owner when you are unsure. Lazur makes no compliance certification claim on this page, and you should not assume one.
Mistakes people make with an AI assistant on the job

items: Trusting a draft without checking dates, names and asset IDs. Small slips reach vendors and tenants.
Asking it to make a change. Lazur guides and drafts. You click, type and send.
Dictating names and codes, then sending without a read. Dictation is only as good as the spelling you check.
Pasting a whole tenant list into a question. Ask about the screen in front of you instead.
Expecting it to know your building. It reads what is on screen, so keep the asset list open when you ask.
Skipping real work. Test it on one repeated task for a few days before you decide.

blocks.text: Most of these mistakes have one fix. Keep the source open and check the output against it before anything leaves your desk.
Platform limits and when this is not the right tool

Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. If your team works only in a web-based maintenance system on Windows, Lazur is not the fit yet. Your maintenance product may also have its own system requirements. Check them with the vendor before you build a workflow around it.
What to do next, starting this week

items: Download Lazur for Mac from the [download page](/download).
Pick one repeated task, such as the vendor reply or the PM sheet check.
Hold Option and Command and ask about one screen you use every day. Notice what it points at.
Check your employer's data rules before you paste any tenant or staff record.
Compare the plans on the [pricing page](/pricing) before you commit.

faq.question: Is Lazur an AI assistant for facilities managers, or a plugin for Excel and Outlook?
faq.answer: Lazur is a voice assistant for Mac. It is not a plugin or add-in for Excel, Outlook or any other app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. It sees your screen while you hold Option and Command, answers out loud, points at things, guides you through steps and drafts or dictates text.

faq.question: Will Lazur update my work order system or send vendor emails for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. It can draft the email and type dictated text at the cursor. You review the text, make the change and send it yourself.

faq.question: Does it work with CMMS or CAFM software?
faq.answer: Lazur can help with anything that is on your screen, including a web-based system, while you hold the shortcut. I could not verify Mac or browser support for specific facilities products. Check each vendor's system requirements before you rely on a workflow.

faq.question: Can I use it with tenant or staff data?
faq.answer: Only if your employer's rules allow it. Lazur looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer and are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Your employer's policy still decides what you may share.

faq.question: Do I need to know Excel well to use it?
faq.answer: No, but you need to know what you want to change. Ask Lazur to explain a formula, or to guide you through a menu path such as Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules > Less Than. Test every change on a copy of the sheet first.

faq.question: Is the research reliable enough for vendor choices?
faq.answer: Use research to find sources, not to make the decision. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs and returns a summary and a report. Open each page yourself, check its date, and confirm prices on the vendor's own pricing page.

faq.question: What does it cost, and is there a trial?
faq.answer: There is a free trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Check the current plans and limits on the pricing page before you buy.

painPoints.title: Work orders take the biggest share
painPoints.text: In a 2025 VTS survey, just over 60% of property managers and business leaders named work order management as a top time drain. The survey counts shares, not hours, so use it as a pattern rather than a measure of your week.

painPoints.title: Invoices and vendor follow-up pile up
painPoints.text: The same survey found 40% name invoice and payment processing, and 38% name vendor coordination. Each one means chasing replies, matching totals and fixing the same spreadsheet again.

painPoints.title: Too many systems, not enough matching data
painPoints.text: Property managers in the same coverage average five operational systems and three reporting tools a day. About one-third say they waste time on cross-system data that does not line up.

painPoints.title: An inbox that never empties
painPoints.text: Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index reports an average of 117 emails received per day for knowledge workers. Most get skimmed in under 60 seconds. That is a general office figure, not a facilities one.

painPoints.title: Interruptions that break the plan
painPoints.text: Microsoft's text says people are interrupted about every 2 minutes. Its methodology gives 275 interruptions a day for the top 20% of users by ping volume. The two figures conflict, so treat them as a rough sign of constant switching.
